My land here in Quzhou is about 10 mu. I've been farming this same plot since I was young, watching my father do it, and I know what works here. The soil is sandy loam, the wells are getting deeper every year, but the land still produces if you treat it right.

I'll do what I always do — wheat in winter, corn in summer on the same land. Everyone around here does this. It fits the season, the market, the equipment I share with my cousin. I don't want to experiment with cotton or vegetables. Those need more knowledge, more trips to market, more labor. At my age I'm not changing what works.

For seeds, I'll buy the improved wheat variety from the township supply co-op — probably Jimai or something similar to what the neighbors are using. For corn, I'll buy hybrid seed like Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu. The hybrid costs more but the yield is better, and I've learned that lesson already.

Fertilizer: I put on plenty. My father always said don't be stingy with the land. I'll apply compound fertilizer at sowing and add urea when the wheat is jointing. Same for corn — urea at the big bell stage.

Irrigation: I'll pump from my tube well. Wheat needs water at sowing, before winter freeze, at green-up, jointing, and heading — five times to be safe if rain is short. Corn I'll water at sowing if it's dry, then at silking and grain fill.

I'll plough deep before the wheat goes in — that's the proper way. For corn, I'll just rotary till after the wheat harvest because time is short between the two crops.
